title: Sample project: pricing page redesign (fictional)

first_insight.text: The user narrowed scope twice and rejected the first layout, while the AI drafted copy and code the user then reviewed.
first_insight.why: Two chat turns show scope being narrowed and one shows a draft being rejected, and commits follow each decision.

findings.text: The user set the acceptance criteria (three tiers, no annual toggle) before any implementation began.
The user rejected the first layout and asked for a simpler comparison table, after which the AI produced a revised version.
Commits touching the pricing page follow each approved draft within the same day, which fits a review-then-commit sequence.
Copy for the free tier was changed by the user after the AI's draft, as shown by a later commit message.
The notes file records a decision to defer billing integration, with the reason stated.

unknowns: Whether any decisions were made in meetings or messages outside the supplied evidence.
Who wrote each individual line of code. Commits show what changed, not who typed it.
Whether the design tool was used. No design file was supplied.

evidence.label: Chat with Claude, opening request
evidence.excerpt: I want three tiers and no annual toggle. The page should load fast and the comparison should fit on one screen.

evidence.label: Chat with Claude, scope change
evidence.excerpt: Drop the testimonials section for now. We only need pricing and the comparison.

evidence.label: Chat with Claude, layout feedback
evidence.excerpt: This layout is too busy. Make the comparison a plain table and remove the icons.

evidence.label: Commit: add pricing page with three tiers
Commit: replace cards with comparison table
Commit: rewrite free tier copy
evidence.excerpt: Rewrite free tier copy; the draft overpromised support.

evidence.label: Project notes, decisions
evidence.excerpt: Decision: defer billing integration until the page ships. Reason: scope.
